messages:

Subject: Enclave onboarding: connectivity, KMS proof, egress rules

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We're starting the enclave activation for GreenLine's staging environment and I wanted to capture the items we need to satisfy before the smoke run:

- Network allowlist for outbound to S3 (us-west-2) and Redwood telemetry endpoints
- Proof of KMS rotation policy and the customer-managed key ARN
- Egress restrictions (what ports/protocols Redwood expects to be open)
- Service account / IAM role mappings for the runtime to call our object store

I'm attaching a preliminary connectivity matrix (CSV) — ping me if the columns don't line up with what you need. We aim to have this ready ahead of a smoke run on Friday.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Infrastructure Lead, GreenLine Medical
[attachment: greenline-connectivity-matrix.csv (csv)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <infra@greenlinemed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enclave onboarding: connectivity, KMS proof, egress rules

Alex — thanks for the matrix and the summary. Below is a compact acceptance checklist we need to mark pass before we run a smoke test in staging:

1) Network & routing
   - Validate outbound allowlist: S3 (arn endpoints) + telemetry (telemetry.redwood.com:443) — please provide CIDR/DNS entries.
   - NAT/egress IPs: we need the public egress IPs you'll use for the tenant so we can add to our ACLs.
   - Subnet tagging: identify which subnets are control-plane vs runtime; runtime subnets must allow ephemeral outbound to 443 and 80.

2) KMS & keys
   - Customer-managed key ARN (copy of key policy) and a statement of rotation cadence (recommended: 90d).
   - Evidence: KMS rotation policy export (PDF) or a screenshot from the KMS console.

3) Identity & permissions
   - IAM role ARNs and the minimal permissions list for object store access (GetObject, PutObject).
   - Service account email for telemetry ingestion.

4) Egress & firewall
   - Ports required on egress: 443 (TLS) and 80 (optional); if you enforce narrow ranges for ephemeral ports, list them.
   - Any enterprise proxy in the path? If so, provide proxy host and certificate thumbprint.

5) Evidence artifacts
   - Connectivity proof: traceroutes/tcpdump logs that show reachability to our telemetry and S3 endpoints.
   - Network diagram (png/pdf) showing NAT and internet egress.

If you can upload the KMS rotation PDF and the connectivity proof (text) to the Drive link I listed in related links, we'll pick these up and do a quick review. I attached a small sample Terraform snippet that Ben and I use to validate egress rules — optional.

If anything in the matrix is different than the above, call it out and we'll adjust the acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Customer Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0192
[attachment: sample-terraform-egress.tf (tf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Alex Mercer <infra@greenlinemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Apr 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enclave onboarding: connectivity, KMS proof, egress rules

Adding a couple of operational clarifications based on previous tenant activations:

- Please ensure runtime subnets are tagged with "redwood-runtime=true" and control subnets with "redwood-control=true" — our automation uses those tags for provisioning internal routes.
- Telemetry uses TLS to telemetry.redwood.com:443 from the runtime; if you have an outbound proxy, make sure it allows CONNECT to that host (SNI preserved).
- If the tenant is behind a corporate proxy that terminates TLS, we need the proxy certificate chain uploaded so our agents can validate certificate pinning.

I've attached a tiny script we use to produce a connectivity proof that shows TCP handshake to our endpoints (output is a short text file). Alex, if you run that in a pod in the runtime subnets and paste the output we'll consider the connectivity evidence valid for the smoke run.

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood
[attachment: network-access-proof.txt (txt)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Alex — quick summary of Redwood acceptance criteria and next steps to keep this moving:

Acceptance (all must be present)
- Connectivity matrix with CIDRs + proof run (network-access-proof.txt)
- KMS key ARN + rotation policy PDF (kms-rotation-policy.pdf)
- IAM role ARNs with minimal permissions list
- Public egress IP(s) or confirmed NAT translation table

Next steps
1) Upload the four artifacts to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood/inbox/greenline/onboard/runbook-v1 (I've dropped a checklist in the folder).
2) Once uploaded, we'll run a 30-minute review and then schedule a 60-minute smoke test window (we propose Friday 2025-04-25 11:00-12:00 PDT).
3) If all passes, we'll request a quick DocuSign approval to finalize the staging activation.

I'll tentatively reserve the Friday slot; confirm availability and upload times and we'll lock it.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
